paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 11/14/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, Polymarket pays 47.35 and Kalshi 52.00. In polls with fieldwork up to 11/05, she is first in all 57 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, at 30.5% to 38%, and leads in the 29 runoff match-ups in which she was tested, at 52% to 70%. Her appeal to the Cour de cassation against her ineligibility is due to be ruled on by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 17.2 across 42 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days and places in the top two in 51 of the 57 lists of the last 45 days; in the 10 runoff match-ups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, at 30% to 34%. In the win contract, he is at 13.50 on Polymarket and 12.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names among the top five in both markets appear in few lists of the poll database or in none.** David Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 17.05, and at 15.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he appears in 16 of the 57 lists of the last 45 days, without placing in the top two in any of them, and averages 7.6 across 14 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days. Christine Lagarde is 4th on Polymarket, at 7.25, and at 6.00 on Kalshi; no list in the database tests her. The first poll to include her, by Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 11/09 and 11/10, has been reported since 11/11, and its notice entered the list published by the Commission des sondages on 11/12. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 10/29, the European Central Bank announced that she will leave the bank's presidency on 02/07/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 11/09, is at 1.85 on Polymarket and 2.00 on Kalshi; no list in the database tests him, and the notice of the OpinionWay poll for CNews that includes him, with fieldwork from 11/10 to 11/12, entered the Commission's list on 11/14.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are close in the poll average and far apart in the Polymarket win contract.** Philippe averages 14.0 over the last 30 days, across 29 lists from 7 pollsters, and Glucksmann 13.6, across 39 lists from 7 pollsters; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe places in the top two in 3 of 39, and Glucksmann in 3 of 52. In the win contract, Philippe is at 6.50 on Polymarket and 5.30 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 1.65 and 3.00.

**In the French press on 11/14, four of the ten headlines in the latest collection, from 7 outlets, are about Teddy Riner.** Le Monde and RTL report that he says he is not a Macronist and calls Emmanuel Macron's congratulations on his candidacy a "poisoned kiss"; BFMTV reports that he says Macron did not launch his candidacy; and CNews carries his statement that he belongs to no political family. Three headlines, from Le Monde, BFMTV and Le Parisien, are about Gérard Larcher's invitation to the candidates of the right and centre to a meeting to settle a method for choosing between them. Le JDD runs a roundup of the day's economic news that includes the election.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
